sub_questions.question: Why did my credit balance drop faster this week even though my usage didn't change?

claims.claim: Credits are not charged at a flat rate per response.
claims.guide_evidence: Message credits are not consumed at a flat rate.

claims.claim: Lighter models can cost as little as 1 credit per response.
claims.guide_evidence: lighter models (for example smaller GPT variants) consume as little as 1 credit per response

claims.claim: Mid-tier models cost around 5 credits per response.
Heavier or multimodal models (transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) cost around 10 credits per response.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models (audio transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: A shift in model mix toward heavier models could explain faster credit burn without any change in request volume.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: The app or its users may have been using a heavier model more often this week.
Checking usage logs for which model handled the most requests will confirm the cause.

evaluation.rationale: The guide supports the per-model credit rates and the idea that heavier models use up credits faster, and the answer frames this as a possible cause rather than a confirmed one. However, it guesses that the customer's model mix changed, even though she said nothing changed, and it points her to "usage logs," which the guide never mentions. It also doesn't ask for details like which apps or models she uses. These issues are minor and unlikely to cause harm.
